body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 6a40e3b60ed70f06c1a51a645036e20316b886d7 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (High-tier review, safety floor: STEP import fidelity and gouge verdicts.)

### What looks good
- **The flag follows the facets on every import path.** `ImportModel::new` (GUI worker, script `cam.import`, MCP `import_model`, which calls `api::v_import`), `UpdateModel` (`with_fidelity` on GUI, script/MCP and `ImportFixture` re-imports), fresh `ImportFixture` (it carries the `ImportModel`), `AddFixtureModel`, and the project loader (`project/apply.rs:655`). Undo restores `prev_coarse_mm` (`update_model.rs:184`). `DeleteEntity` snapshots it and puts it back. `RepairModel` keeps it (`keeping_fidelity`). The generated-mesh updates (built-in vise, accessory, `SetPlate`) clear it, which is right: their facets are exact. I found no path that resets a coarse mesh to "full fidelity" without replacing its facets.
- **Every tightening points the safe way.** `excess_floor` only shrinks a tolerance, and returns `None` (refuse) once nothing is left.
  - (b) floor: `section.rs:104`. #942's whole-arc reading and #839's union joints use the same `floor` variable, and both are pinned.
  - (b2) `allow`: `section.rs:283`.
  - (f) gouge gate: `gate - excess`; the rest half is unchanged. `finish.rs:104`.
  - `contain_into` and the lathe axial hole: `generate.rs:2963` and `generate.rs:3222`.
  - `deviate` at `verdict_tol`: in both `simulate_document` and `stock_sim_carry::judge`.
- **The generator and the gate read the same numbers.** `material.excess` comes from `excess_of(src)`, and `op_problem` reads the same source names through `op_coarse` (stock copied from a model included). `floor_of = min(finish_tol, GOUGE_TOL)` is exactly where the envelope law stops tightening, so an op whose envelope reads untightened is always refused.
- **Refusal is binding on every post path.** `verification_report` (single file, per-op files and per-mount) starts with `gate_problems`. When the per-op list is empty, `verdict_tol`'s error is still pushed as a problem. That covers a part no op names, and does not depend on `sim_clause`'s `uncovered` rule. MCP `post` and the script API go through the same report.
- **Cached paths cannot slip through.** A cached path from before a coarser re-import is stale: the facets changed, so the rev and stamp changed. Undo trades facets and flag together, so a restored stamp always matches the flag it was judged under.
- **Fixtures are handled conservatively.** The box grows by the full chord on every side, and the mesh is never offered to the acquitting mesh law.
- **No-op for normal models.** No golden, snapshot or testdata file is in the diff (`git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat`; `solid_law_goldens.rs` gains one `..Default::default()` line only). `coarse_mm` uses `skip_serializing_if`, and the byte-for-byte save is pinned.
- **Law checks.**
  - No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside `#[cfg(test)]`.
  - New modules carry provenance lines and are under 400 lines. `generate.rs` shrank (the `finish_tol_of` move).
  - Tests live in the owning crates. No new crate dependency.
  - The decision file is present, there is a `Changelog:` line, and the body ends `Fixes #864`.
- **Units are honest.** The chord is scaled by `|mm_per_unit|` after tessellation. The inch fixture is pinned as not flagged. A metre file reads 0.01 mm, which leaves 0.005 mm. The 1e-9 slack in `step::coarse` only absorbs the unit round trip.

### Local results (worktree at 6a40e3b6; `origin/main` e0cb0049 merges in as "Already up to date")
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests` | 55 binaries, 432 passed, 0 failed |
| app `model_fidelity` | 9 passed |
| app lib `step_refine::tests` | 4 passed |
| app `step_fidelity` / `step_chord_units` / `import` | 2 / 3 / 23 passed |
| app `verify_arc_reading` / `boundary_arc_walls` | 7 / 4 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` / `commands_undo` | 71 / 30 passed |
| app `tool_body_bands` / `tool_body_judged` | 13 / 8 passed |
| app `golden_cl` / `conformance` | 25 / 6 passed |
| app `mcp_setup` / `mcp_model` | 6 / 5 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`, includes `tests::model_fidelity`) | 531 passed, 5 ignored |
| clippy `-p sim -p app -p ui -p motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the release tier and the heavy `--ignored` lanes, the motion test suites (motion has only `..Default::default()` edits; clippy covered it), and the snapshot PNGs (release lane).

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
1. **The unchanged collision laws are an acceptable residual, not a blocker.**
   - While an op still posts, `excess < floor_of <= GOUGE_TOL = 0.01 mm`, so the kept chord is under 0.015 mm against the promised 0.005 mm.
   - The reach (c, c3), rapids (d), turning-rapid and bar-feed/holder scans can therefore read at most 0.01 mm more generous than on a full-fidelity model. That is the size of the margin those laws already grant (`gouge_tol`), and it is on a convex wall only.
   - The final program sim, which does judge material removal, is tightened.
   - It is bounded, documented in the PR and in #904, and not silent. A gross collision is not hidden by 0.01 mm.
   - Since this is about collisions, #904 may deserve P1 rather than P2 for item 2.
2. **Older project files.** A file saved before this PR with an over-budget mesh loads as full fidelity. No chord is stored, and nothing re-checks it on load (the mesh alone cannot say). That matches the pre-PR verdict, so it is no regression; a re-import is the only cure. An older build opening a new file ignores `coarse_mm` (the DTO has no `deny_unknown_fields`) and judges as it always did. Both could be one line in the release notes.
3. **Orphaned stock copy.** A `FromModel` stock whose source model was deleted keeps the coarse facets but reads excess 0 (`coarse_source` resolves through the source name). The part verdicts are unaffected (the parts carry their own flag); only ops on that stock lose the tightening. Worth a line in #904.
4. **Very small tolerances can give false gouge lines.** Near the refusal edge (excess just under 0.01 mm) the program sim judges at a tolerance close to zero. Grid noise on an exactly finished face could then read as a false "gouge" line rather than the named refusal. It is the safe side, but the message misleads. #904 could consider a minimum honest tolerance (for example refuse below 0.001 mm).
5. **Wording.** "Re-import with a larger budget" is not actionable yet: there is no budget setting (#904). The model-page hint says so in effect ("too large to import at full detail"), but a user may look for a setting that does not exist. Until #904 lands, consider adding "(the budget is not adjustable yet)" to the hint and MCP `note`. The rest is plain English.
6. **`step::with_facet_budget`.** It is `pub` + `#[doc(hidden)]`, not `cfg(test)`. It only lowers the budget and is thread-local, so it is harmless.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
